rows.subtype: Approach: prioritising by urgent versus important [Thinking]
rows.description: Facing a test in three days and a district match on Saturday, the student separates what is due soon from what matters long term, and drops a lower-value gaming session while keeping sport.

rows.subtype: Approach: promising to cut screens completely [Pitfall]
rows.description: A student swears to delete all games and social apps. The all-or-nothing rule lasts four days, then a single slip is treated as total failure and the old habit returns at full strength.

rows.subtype: Approach: tracking actual screen time first [Action]
rows.description: Using the phone's usage report for a week, the student discovers three hours a day on short videos, far more than he guessed. The data, not a lecture, makes him ready to change.

rows.subtype: Approach: if-then rules for phone use [Thinking]
rows.description: The student sets a rule: if study session starts, then phone goes into the hall drawer; if the timer ends, then phone returns. A concrete trigger works better than general willpower.

rows.subtype: Approach: treating sport as reward only after study [Pitfall]
rows.description: The student makes football contingent on finishing all revision. Study runs late every day, sport disappears, mood falls, and concentration gets worse rather than better.

rows.description: The student notices that hard subjects go best before dinner and that a run clears her head, so she places a short run before the hardest study block instead of treating exercise as a competitor.

rows.subtype: Approach: accountability partner for screen limits [Action]
rows.description: Two friends message each other a screenshot of daily screen time each night. The small social stakes make the limit feel real, and comparing numbers turns it into a friendly challenge.

rows.subtype: Approach: reviewing and loosening an unrealistic plan [Revision]
rows.description: After two weeks of missing targets, the student sees the schedule left no room for travel or festivals. He trims study blocks slightly, keeps sport fixed and allows one guilt-free screen evening.
